candidate.educational_objective: Recognize common causes of eosinophilia and avoid overinterpreting a single laboratory finding.

options.A: Eosinophilia can occur with allergic disorders; parasitic infections are another important cause.
options.B: Eosinophilia is specific for acute bacterial infection.
options.D: The result cannot occur with allergic disease.

candidate.rationale: Eosinophilia is associated with allergic disorders such as asthma and hay fever and can also occur with parasitic infections, drug reactions, and other conditions. It is not specific for one diagnosis.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Eosinophilia commonly accompanies allergic disease and parasitic infection but is not diagnostic of a single disorder.
candidate.source_locator: Etiology—secondary eosinophilia from allergic disorders and parasitic infestations
candidate.stem: A client with asthma and seasonal allergic symptoms has an elevated eosinophil count. Which interpretation is most appropriate?
